title: No estoy de acuerdo
blurbEn: Arguing with Diego about nothing in particular, and the set phrases that make disagreement possible.
body:
Diego y yo discutimos casi todos los días, siempre de cosas sin importancia: el café, el fútbol, la mejor manera de aprender un idioma.

—Los idiomas se aprenden mejor viajando —dice.

—No estoy de acuerdo. Se aprenden mejor estudiando y luego viajando.

—Eso es lo mismo.

—No lo es en absoluto.

Discutir en español es un ejercicio útil, porque tiene sus propias fórmulas. «Estoy de acuerdo contigo». «Tienes razón, pero...». «Depende». «Ya, bueno». «No lo veo así».

Esa última es mi favorita: suena educada y significa exactamente lo contrario.

Diego usa mucho «ya, bueno», que en la práctica quiere decir «no pienso seguir hablando de esto».

Nunca nos enfadamos de verdad. Sería aburridísimo. Es un deporte, no una guerra, y como todo deporte tiene reglas que nadie ha escrito.

Al final siempre acabamos de acuerdo en algo distinto de lo que discutíamos.
translationEn:
Diego and I argue almost every day, always about unimportant things: coffee, football, the best way to learn a language.

"Languages are learned better by travelling," he says.

"I don't agree. They're learned better by studying and then travelling."

"That's the same thing."

"It absolutely is not."

Arguing in Spanish is a useful exercise, because it has its own set phrases. "I agree with you." "You're right, but..." "It depends." "Yeah, well." "I don't see it that way."

That last one is my favourite: it sounds polite and means exactly the opposite.

Diego uses "ya, bueno" a lot, which in practice means "I don't intend to keep talking about this".

We never really fall out. It would be incredibly boring. It's a sport, not a war, and like every sport it has rules nobody has written down.

In the end we always end up agreeing on something different from what we were arguing about.

de acuerdo.note: 'estar de acuerdo con' is to agree with. Never 'estoy acuerdo'.

en absoluto.note: Despite the word, it is emphatically negative: 'not at all'.

Ya, bueno.note: Formally an agreement; in practice it closes a conversation down.

phrases.gloss: I don't see it that way
